chapters.lede: Digital citizenship, academic integrity, responsible AI, acceptable use, social media and devices — one network baseline, and clear room for each school's local choices.

blocks.title: Law and Cambridge come first
blocks.text: Apply current law and **current Cambridge assessment regulations** where relevant. For Cambridge coursework and other Cambridge-assessed work, always check the current Cambridge Handbook, the component instructions and current generative-AI guidance. Localise the package before it reaches students and parents.
check: Apply applicable law and current Cambridge assessment regulations where relevant
Do not distribute raw implementation templates or agreements to students/parents

chapters.title: The teacher sets the AI level for every task
chapters.lede: AI use must serve a learning objective, be transparent, and never bypass learning. Permission is decided task by task.

blocks.title: Five task-based AI permission levels
blocks.intro: The teacher states the level for **each** task. Permission for one task does not carry over to another.

items.name: Only the parts the teacher names

check: The teacher must state the permitted AI level for each task
AI use is part of the learning objective and follows teacher directions

blocks.title: No level stated = NO AI
blocks.text: If the teacher has not stated an AI level, **NO AI** applies to submitted work. Disclosure is a separate rule: whenever AI contributes ideas, wording, research, code or substantive edits, it must be disclosed. **Not disclosing when required is academic misconduct.**
check: If no AI level is stated, NO AI applies to submitted work
Failure to disclose AI use when required constitutes academic misconduct

blocks.title: Staff and AI
do: Check accuracy, syllabus fit, level, bias and age-appropriateness before using AI material.
Use only tools on the school's **Approved AI Tools List**.
Stay responsible for every AI-drafted email, report or piece of feedback.
dont: Enter personal information into unapproved AI tools.
Upload identifiable student work to unapproved AI services.
Assume one age threshold applies to every AI service.

source.at: Staff use; Data and age rules

check: Do not enter personal information into general-purpose or unapproved AI tools
Do not assume one age threshold applies to every AI service

blocks.title: Safeguarding is never just a tech violation
blocks.text: Online harm, sextortion, synthetic sexual content (including deepfakes) and cyberbullying go to the **Safeguarding Lead** — they must not be treated only as technology violations. Student use of AI companion or relationship bots is not permitted in school-related contexts.
check: Safeguarding concerns must not be treated only as technology violations
Student use of AI companion/relationship bots is not permitted in school-related contexts

chapters.title: Launching the package in your school
chapters.lede: The Implementation Toolkit turns the policies into school-level actions. Localise names, contacts and tools before anything reaches students and parents.

blocks.title: A 30–60–90 day pathway
blocks.intro: An implementation sequence, not a network deadline.

steps.name: Align
steps.text: Assign roles, review the package and local policies, confirm the device / BYOD model, create the **Approved AI Tools List**.

steps.name: Localise & communicate
steps.text: Finalise the local AUP, privacy notice, incident route, smartphone procedures. Brief staff first, then families.

steps.name: Implement & review
steps.text: Apply controls, sample classroom consistency, review incidents and gaps, set next-term priorities.

check: the pathway is an implementation guide, not a network deadline

blocks.title: Who owns what
rows: Principal / leadership
Approves the local model, assigns roles, approves local policies and exceptions
Digital Citizenship Coordinator
Implementation, staff communication, student and parent education
AI Integration Coordinator
The Approved AI Tools List (reviewed **at least once per term**), AI literacy, developmental AI self-assessment
Privacy / Data-Protection Lead
Privacy notice, consent, retention, DPIA coordination
Safeguarding Lead
Online harm, exploitation, sextortion, synthetic sexual content, cyberbullying
IT / MDM Lead
Approved technical controls — **IT does not create policy**
Teachers
Task-level AI rules, consistent device expectations, protecting student data
